entries.template: A shop has {choiceA} shirt designs and {choiceB} trouser designs. How many different shirt-trouser outfits can be formed?
A canteen offers {choiceA} starters and {choiceB} main courses. If one of each is chosen, how many meal combinations are possible?
There are {choiceA} roads from village A to village B and {choiceB} roads from village B to village C. How many routes from A to C pass through B?
A stationery counter has {choiceA} pen colours and {choiceB} notebook-cover designs. How many pen-and-notebook pairs can be made?
A school uniform may use any of {choiceA} shirt patterns with any of {choiceB} tie patterns. How many uniforms are possible?
A phone is available in {choiceA} models, and each model has {choiceB} compatible case designs. How many model-case choices are available?
A certificate can carry one of {choiceA} border designs and one of {choiceB} seal designs. How many certificate layouts are possible?
A student chooses one of {choiceA} elective subjects and one of {choiceB} activity clubs. How many subject-club choices are possible?
A meal consists of one of {choiceA} starters, one of {choiceB} main courses and one of {choiceC} desserts. How many complete meals can be ordered?
A product bundle contains one of {choiceA} devices, one of {choiceB} protection plans and one of {choiceC} delivery slots. How many bundles are possible?
A traveller must choose one of {choiceA} first-leg trains, one of {choiceB} connecting buses and one of {choiceC} final-leg taxis. How many complete journeys are possible?
A team jersey is specified by one of {choiceA} colours, one of {choiceB} sizes and one of {choiceC} number styles. How many jersey variants are possible?
A training plan uses one of {choiceA} modules, one of {choiceB} instructors and one of {choiceC} assessment slots. Every combination is permitted. How many plans are possible?
For a three-stage service request, a customer selects one of {choiceA} service types, one of {choiceB} centres and one of {choiceC} appointment windows. How many requests can be formed?
A passenger can travel by any of {choiceA} bus routes or any of {choiceB} train routes. If exactly one route is chosen, how many choices are available?
A library member may borrow one book from {choiceA} history titles or one from {choiceB} science titles. How many single-book choices are possible?
A student may enter one of {choiceA} indoor events or one of {choiceB} outdoor events. How many event choices are available?
An applicant may select one of {choiceA} morning interview slots or one of {choiceB} afternoon slots. How many slots can be selected?
A customer can choose one of {choiceA} prepaid plans or one of {choiceB} postpaid plans. How many plans are available in all?
A candidate must answer exactly one optional question, chosen from {choiceA} questions in Section A or {choiceB} questions in Section B. How many choices are possible?
A grant application may be submitted under one of {choiceA} academic schemes, one of {choiceB} sports schemes or one of {choiceC} cultural schemes. How many schemes are available?
A traveller chooses exactly one departure: one of {choiceA} buses, {choiceB} trains or {choiceC} flights. How many departures are possible?
A school allows one optional project from {choiceA} science topics, {choiceB} commerce topics or {choiceC} humanities topics. How many project choices are there?
A participant may register for exactly one workshop from {choiceA} technical sessions, {choiceB} management sessions or {choiceC} communication sessions. How many registrations are possible?

A traveller can go through town X in {caseAFirst} ways and then continue in {caseARest} ways, or go through town Y in {caseBFirst} ways and then continue in {caseBRest} ways. How many routes are possible?

A meal may be vegetarian with {caseAFirst} main-course choices and {caseARest} side choices, or non-vegetarian with {caseBFirst} main-course choices and {caseBRest} side choices. How many meals are possible?

A sports kit may be a cricket kit with {caseAFirst} shirt choices and {caseARest} cap choices, or a football kit with {caseBFirst} shirt choices and {caseBRest} cap choices. How many kits are possible?

A student can take a science project with {caseAFirst} topic choices and {caseARest} mentor choices, or a commerce project with {caseBFirst} topic choices and {caseBRest} mentor choices. How many topic-mentor assignments are possible?

A service package may be standard with {caseAFirst} plan choices and {caseARest} add-on choices, or premium with {caseBFirst} plan choices and {caseBRest} add-on choices. How many packages are possible?

A commuter may cross by bridge using {caseAFirst} entry roads and {caseARest} exit roads, or by tunnel using {caseBFirst} entry roads and {caseBRest} exit roads. How many complete crossings are possible?

A candidate may attend a morning session with {caseAFirst} rooms and {caseARest} reporting slots, or an evening session with {caseBFirst} rooms and {caseBRest} reporting slots. How many room-slot choices are possible?

A customer may buy a basic device with {caseAFirst} colour choices and {caseARest} warranty plans, or a pro device with {caseBFirst} colour choices and {caseBRest} warranty plans. How many purchases are possible?

An exam candidate may choose Section A with {caseAFirst} question sets and {caseARest} language versions, or Section B with {caseBFirst} question sets and {caseBRest} language versions. How many valid section-version choices are possible?

A delivery can use the northern hub with {caseAFirst} incoming routes and {caseARest} outgoing routes, or the southern hub with {caseBFirst} incoming routes and {caseBRest} outgoing routes. How many hub-based routes are possible?
A shop can form {choiceA} shirt-trouser pairs from each of {choiceB} display groups, but {invalidChoices} pairs are unavailable. How many pairs remain available?
There are {choiceA} first-leg routes and {choiceB} second-leg routes. If {invalidChoices} complete routes are closed, how many routes remain?
A canteen can combine {choiceA} main courses with {choiceB} drinks. If {invalidChoices} combinations contain an unavailable item, how many valid combinations remain?
A device bundle pairs {choiceA} models with {choiceB} accessories. If {invalidChoices} model-accessory pairs are incompatible, how many compatible bundles are possible?
A registration form offers {choiceA} course choices and {choiceB} time slots. If {invalidChoices} course-slot pairs are already full, how many pairs remain?
A badge can use {choiceA} emblems and {choiceB} ribbon designs. If {invalidChoices} combinations are reserved, how many unreserved badges can be made?
A booking system combines {choiceA} service types with {choiceB} appointment windows. After excluding {invalidChoices} prohibited type-window pairs, how many valid bookings remain?
A training portal combines {choiceA} modules with {choiceB} assessment slots. If {invalidChoices} module-slot pairs violate scheduling rules, how many valid plans remain?
A shop can form {totalChoices} shirt-trouser outfits. If there are {knownChoices} shirt designs and every shirt can be paired with every trouser design, how many trouser designs are there?
A menu has {totalChoices} starter-main-course combinations. If {knownChoices} starters are available and every starter can be paired with every main course, how many main courses are available?
There are {totalChoices} routes from A to C through B. If there are {knownChoices} roads from A to B and every such road can connect to every road from B to C, how many roads run from B to C?
A badge system produces {totalChoices} emblem-ribbon combinations. If {knownChoices} emblems are available, how many ribbon designs are there?
A college offers {totalChoices} subject-slot combinations. If there are {knownChoices} subjects and each is offered in the same set of slots, how many slots are available?
A service catalogue contains {totalChoices} plan-add-on combinations. If {knownChoices} plans can each use every add-on, how many add-ons are available?

If n = {n}, what is the value of (n - 1)!?
Evaluate 0! + {factorialArgument}!.
Find the value of {factorialArgument}! - 1!.
Simplify ({upper}!)/({lower}!).
If n = {n}, evaluate (n + 1)!/n!.
If n = {n}, evaluate (n + 2)!/n!.
If n! = {target}, find n.
If (n + 1)! = {target}, find n.
If n!/(n - 2)! = {target}, find n.
